text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Rhone Poulenc announces buyout of an outstanding 31.7 percent stake in Rhone Poulenc Rorer, plans to sell part of its chemicals activities.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin seeks to balance employment with the need to stabilise budget deficits, but does not commit himself to any deficit target figure.
-- Defence Minister Alain Richard to carry on defence industry restructuring, sees room for only one passenger and military aircraft manufacturer in Europe.
-- Generale des Eaux to invest 870 million francs in British railroads.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn does not rule out some privatisations, notably for companies involved in European-wide operations.
-- Citroen car manufacturer posts a 2.69 billion francs loss for 1996.
-- Havas considers selling weeklies Le Point and L'Express, chairman Pierre Dauzier expects a 1.5 billion franc profit for 1997.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government considers cutting interest rate offered on housing savings scheme PEL and personal savings scheme Livret A of up to 0.5 percent. Livret A currently offers 3.5 percent.
-- CGIP to decide before end July whether to increase its 20 percent stake in Cap Gemini.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- France has an unofficial 1997 defiict target of 3.3 percent, an unnamed senior official is quoted as saying.
-- Thomson-CSF former computer maintenance subsidiary Thomainfor, sold to a U.S.-based group in February, has been placed under legal administration by a court.
-- Employment and Solidarity Minister Martine Aubry criticises layoff plan in "a large automobile firm" for its lack of retraining measures.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin spokesman denies reports of France Telecom sale, adds no decision has been made.
